title: The system: a food-delivery platform whose services talk through Kafka
caption: Services only write their own data or produce events; every consumer group reads the same retained log at its own pace.

steps.text: The order service only writes its own database. It never publishes to Kafka itself, so there is no dual write that can half-fail.

A CDC connector tails the database's change log and turns every committed row change into a record on the orders topic, keyed by order_id. Its schema is registered first; an incompatible change is rejected there.
The courier service produces a GPS ping every 4 s per courier to courier-locations, keyed by courier_id, with acks=all.
The cluster splits each topic into partitions, keeps 3 replicas of each on different brokers, and retains records for 7 days whether or not anyone has read them.
A stream processor joins orders with courier positions, computes ETAs and fraud scores, and writes eta-updates back to Kafka.
Three consumer groups read the same records independently, each at its own offset: analytics to the lake, the indexer to search, the notifier to customers' phones.

scenarios.name: Dinner rush
scenarios.summary: Producers never slow down for consumers: each group falls behind on its own, and lag tells you which one to scale.

steps.text: At 19:00 orders and GPS pings triple. Producers write at full speed; brokers only append.
The notifier keeps up, but the search indexer's lag climbs to 90 s: its writes to the search cluster are the slow part.
Add indexer instances. They can only help up to the number of partitions; beyond that, extra members sit idle.
Analytics is hours behind and nobody cares: it batches into hourly files anyway. Alert on lag per group, with a different threshold for each.

scenarios.name: Bad indexer deploy
scenarios.summary: Because Kafka keeps the log, a corrupted downstream store is rebuilt by rewinding one group's offset; nobody else is affected.

steps.text: A bug in a new indexer version writes wrong prices into the search index for 2 days.
Ship the fix, stop the group, and reset its committed offsets to the time before the bug (still inside the 7-day retention).
The indexer replays 2 days of orders. Upserts by order id make the replay safe: each document ends up in its latest correct state.
Analytics and notifier never noticed: their offsets didn't move.

scenarios.name: Schema change
scenarios.summary: The registry turns a breaking change into a failed deploy instead of a 3 a.m. consumer crash.

steps.text: The order team adds an optional tip field to the order schema.
The connector registers version 4. It has a default value, so it is backward compatible and accepted.
Old consumers keep reading and ignore the new field; the indexer upgrades when it wants to.
Next month someone tries to rename order_id. The registry rejects the incompatible schema, and the change has to be made as a new field or a new topic.
